title: Your panel now updates itself daily
summary: A signed cyber-news feed refreshes the panel daily, so every persona reacts to this week's breaches, regulation, and vendor moves.
body: Each CISO is grounded in the world that touches their seat. A daily pipeline scrapes public security sources, digests them (key points, never verbatim), signs the bundle, and your instance verifies and applies it — tagged by region and industry so the right personas react to the right news.
why: Major capability that isn't announced in the news center yet.

title: Decision-grade output: a stance, the objections, and the dissent
summary: Not a vibe and a number — a clear stance, the ranked objections that block it, and the segment most against you.
body: Every panel run returns a decision-grade read: a stance, the objections ranked by how much they block adoption, the most-opposed segment, and a statistical check on whether the panel was even the right shape for the question.
why: Core output format, not yet called out as an update.

title: Run 30 to 200 CISOs — your call
summary: Panel size is a dial: 30 for a fast read, up to 200 for a tighter one. The floor of 30 keeps every answer statistically honest.
body: Choose your N. A smaller panel is faster and cheaper; a larger one narrows the confidence band. Below 30 the product refuses — that's the line where the statistics stop being meaningful.
